# Paper Details

**Full Title:** "Adaptive Inference-Time Compute: LLMs Can Predict if They Can Do Better, Even Mid-Generation"

**Authors:** Rohin Manvi, Anikait Singh, Stefano Ermon

**Venue:** arXiv:2410.02725 [cs.CL] — Computer Science > Computation and Language

**Submission Date:** October 3, 2024

**Abstract Summary:**

The researchers propose a self-evaluation mechanism enabling language models to adaptively determine whether generating additional samples would improve performance. Key innovations include:

- Using a generative reward model allowing the LLM to "predict mid-generation the probability that restarting the generation will yield a better response"
- No external reward model required—predictions involve generating a single predefined token
- Training on real LMSYS user prompts with Llama 3.1 8B

**Performance Gains:**
- AlpacaEval win rate against GPT-4: 21% → 34% (with 16 samples)
- GSM8K math performance: 84% → 91%
- 74% of improvements achievable with only 1.2 average samples instead of 16

The approach enables efficient compute utilization through early sample pruning (50-75%) with minimal performance loss.

I found the paper you're looking for! Here's information about "Strategic Scaling of Test-Time Compute: A Bandit Learning Approach":

## Overview

Scaling test-time compute has emerged as an effective strategy for improving the performance of large language models. However, existing methods typically allocate compute uniformly across all queries, overlooking variation in query difficulty.

## The Approach

The paper formulates test-time compute allocation as a novel bandit learning problem and proposes adaptive algorithms that estimate query difficulty on the fly and allocate compute accordingly. Compared to uniform allocation, their algorithms allocate more compute to challenging queries while maintaining accuracy on easier ones.

Among challenging queries, the algorithms further learn to prioritize solvable instances, effectively reducing excessive computing on unsolvable queries.

## Key Distinction from Other Work

Previous methods focus on adaptive allocation within an individual query, without considering opportunities to redistribute compute across a set of queries. In contrast, this work studies strategic compute allocation across multiple queries, introducing an additional layer of optimization—for example, deciding when to transfer unused budget from easier queries to harder ones.

## Results

The paper theoretically proves that the algorithms achieve better compute efficiency than uniform allocation and empirically validates their effectiveness on math and code benchmarks.

- **Authors:** Yang Yue, Zhiqi Chen, Rui Lu, Andrew Zhao, Zhaokai Wang, Shiji Song, Gao Huang

- **Why important:** NeurIPS 2025 Best Paper Runner-Up; directly challenges a foundational assumption about RL for LLM reasoning.
- **Summary:** Shows that RLVR improves sampling efficiency but does not expand the fundamental reasoning capacity of LLMs beyond what the base model already possesses -- reasoning abilities are bounded by the base model, and distillation (not RL) is what genuinely introduces new reasoning patterns.

## PART 2: INFERENCE SCALING LAWS -- KEY PAPERS

---

**7. "Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters"**
- **Authors:** Charlie Snell, Jaehoon Lee, Kelvin Xu, Aviral Kumar
- **Venue:** arXiv preprint (Aug 2024); widely cited foundational paper
- **URL:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.03314
- **Why important:** Seminal paper on test-time compute; over 500+ citations; established the "compute-optimal" test-time scaling paradigm.
- **Summary:** Demonstrates that adaptively allocating test-time compute based on prompt difficulty can outperform best-of-N baselines by 4x and enable a small model to match a 14x larger model. Proposes compute-optimal strategies combining dense reward model search with adaptive distribution updates.

---

**8. "Large Language Monkeys: Scaling Inference Compute with Repeated Sampling"**
- **Authors:** Bradley Brown, Jordan Juravsky, Ryan Ehrlich, Ronald Clark, Quoc V. Le, Christopher Re, Azalia Mirhoseini
- **Venue:** arXiv preprint (Jul 2024); Stanford Scaling Intelligence Lab
- **URL:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.21787
- **Why important:** Highly cited; demonstrates dramatic coverage scaling over 4 orders of magnitude via repeated sampling.
- **Summary:** Shows that coverage (fraction of problems solved by any attempt) scales log-linearly/power-law with number of samples. On SWE-bench Lite, DeepSeek-V2-Coder-Instruct improves from 15.9% (1 sample) to 56% (250 samples). Highlights the critical role of verification in domains where answers can be automatically checked.

---

**9. "Inference Scaling Laws: An Empirical Analysis of Compute-Optimal Inference for Problem-Solving with Language Models"**
- **Authors:** Yangzhen Wu, Zhiqing Sun, Shanda Li, Sean Welleck, Yiming Yang
- **Venue:** ICLR 2025 (published as conference paper)
- **URL:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.00724
- **Why important:** Published at ICLR 2025; establishes Chinchilla-style scaling laws for inference.
- **Summary:** Analyzes trade-offs between model size and inference strategies (greedy, majority voting, best-of-N, tree search). Shows Llemma-7B with a novel REBASE tree search outperforms Llemma-34B across all inference budgets on MATH. Demonstrates that scaling inference compute can be more efficient than scaling model parameters.

---

**10. "s1: Simple test-time scaling"**
- **Authors:** Niklas Muennighoff, Zitong Yang, Weijia Shi, Xiang Lisa Li, Li Fei-Fei, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Luke Zettlemoyer, Percy Liang, Emmanuel Candes, Tatsunori Hashimoto
- **Venue:** EMNLP 2025 (Suzhou, China)
- **URL:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.19393
- **Why important:** Published at EMNLP 2025; open-source reproduction of OpenAI o1 test-time scaling; highly influential.
- **Summary:** Curates a 1,000-example dataset (s1K) selected by difficulty, diversity, and quality. Introduces "budget forcing" to control reasoning depth by terminating or extending thinking. After SFT on Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct, the resulting s1-32B exceeds o1-preview on MATH and AIME24 by up to 27%. Fully open-source.

---

**11. "Provable Scaling Laws for the Test-Time Compute of Large Language Models"**
- **Authors:** Yanxi Chen, Xuchen Pan, Yaliang Li, Bolin Ding, Jingren Zhou
- **Venue:** NeurIPS 2025
- **URL:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.19477
- **Why important:** Accepted at NeurIPS 2025; provides theoretical guarantees for test-time scaling.
- **Summary:** Introduces two verifier-free algorithms (knockout tournament and league evaluation) where the LLM itself serves as the judge. Proves that failure probability decreases exponentially or polynomially as compute increases. No external reward model needed.

---

**12. "A Simple Model of Inference Scaling Laws"**
- **Authors:** Noam Levi
- **Venue:** arXiv preprint (Oct 2024)
- **URL:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.16377
- **Why important:** Provides theoretical framework for understanding pass@k inference scaling.
- **Summary:** Proposes a statistical framework based on memorization to explain pass@k scaling behavior, demonstrating power-law decay in inference loss with increasing trials.

---

**13. "Rethinking Fine-Tuning when Scaling Test-Time Compute: Limiting Confidence Improves Mathematical Reasoning"**
- **Authors:** Feng Chen, Allan Raventos, Nan Cheng, Surya Ganguli, Shaul Druckmann
- **Venue:** NeurIPS 2025 (poster)
- **URL:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.07154
- **Why important:** Accepted at NeurIPS 2025; addresses the training-inference alignment problem for test-time scaling.
- **Summary:** Shows that standard cross-entropy training actually hurts pass@N performance with longer training due to overconfidence. Proposes confidence-limiting training that improves mathematical reasoning under sampling-based test-time compute on MATH and MiniF2F.

---

**14. "Scaling up Test-Time Compute with Latent Reasoning: A Recurrent Depth Approach"**
- **Authors:** Jonas Geiping, Sean McLeish, Neel Jain, John Kirchenbauer, Siddharth Singh, Brian R. Bartoldson, Bhavya Kailkhura, Abhinav Bhatele, Tom Goldstein
- **Venue:** NeurIPS 2025 (poster)
- **URL:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.05171
- **Why important:** NeurIPS 2025; proposes an alternative to chain-of-thought for test-time scaling.
- **Summary:** Scales test-time compute through latent-space iteration via a recurrent block rather than generating more tokens. A 3.5B model achieves reasoning performance of ~50B models, works with small context windows, and can capture reasoning not easily expressed in words.

---

**15. "Test-Time Scaling Makes Overtraining Compute-Optimal"**
- **Authors:** Nicholas Roberts, Sungjun Cho, Zhiqi Gao, Tzu-Heng Huang, Albert Wu, Gabriel Orlanski, Avi Trost, Kelly Buchanan, Aws Albarghouthi, Frederic Sala
- **Venue:** arXiv preprint (Apr 2026)
- **URL:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.01411
- **Why important:** Most recent paper (2026); extends Chinchilla scaling laws to jointly account for inference cost.
- **Summary:** Introduces Train-to-Test (T-squared) scaling laws that jointly optimize model size, training tokens, and inference samples. Shows that when inference cost is accounted for, optimal pretraining shifts radically into the overtraining regime -- smaller, heavily overtrained models become compute-optimal when test-time scaling is used.

---

**16. "Scaling Laws Meet Model Architecture: Toward Inference-Efficient LLMs"**
- **Authors:** Song Bian, Tao Yu, Shivaram Venkataraman, Youngsuk Park
- **Venue:** ICLR 2026
- **URL:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.18245
- **Why important:** Published at ICLR 2026; extends Chinchilla with architecture-conditional scaling laws.
- **Summary:** Introduces conditional scaling laws incorporating architectural factors (hidden size, MLP-to-attention ratio, grouped-query attention). Trained 200+ models (80M-3B params). Optimized architectures achieve up to 2.1% higher accuracy and 42% greater inference throughput vs. LLaMA-3.2.

---

**17. "A Survey of Test-Time Compute: From Intuitive Inference to Deliberate Reasoning"**
- **Authors:** Yixin Ji, Juntao Li, Yang Xiang, Hai Ye, Kaixin Wu, Kai Yao, Jia Xu, Linjian Mo, Min Zhang
- **Venue:** arXiv survey (Jan 2025)
- **URL:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.02497
- **Why important:** Comprehensive survey paper covering the entire test-time compute landscape.
- **Summary:** Taxonomizes test-time compute across System-1 methods (parameter updating, input modification, output calibration) and System-2 methods (repeated sampling, self-correction, tree search). Traces the evolution from fast intuitive inference to deliberate reasoning strategies.

## Overview

"Large Language Monkeys" is a 2024 paper that explores inference compute as a scaling axis by increasing the number of generated samples, as opposed to the traditional focus on training compute.

## Key Findings

Across multiple tasks and models, the research observes that coverage - the fraction of problems solved by any attempt - scales with the number of samples over four orders of magnitude. The work demonstrates that weaker prover policies can effectively improve stronger base models, offering a scalable alternative to dense human annotation.

## Key Research Areas

**1. Solve-Detect-Verify Framework**

A novel approach called FlexiVe introduces a generative verifier that flexibly balances computational resources between fast and slow thinking using a Flexible Allocation of Verification Budget strategy, integrated into a Solve-Detect-Verify pipeline for inference-time scaling. This approach outperforms baselines like self-consistency on challenging mathematical reasoning benchmarks (AIME 2024, AIME 2025, and CNMO).

**2. Adaptive Test-Time Compute Allocation**

Recent research on LLMs like DeepSeek-V3, GPT-4o-mini, and Qwen2.5-7B shows methods that achieve up to 12.8% relative accuracy improvement on MATH under matched budget constraints. The framework uses principled constrained optimization where oracle labels arise from a Lagrangian relaxation of a well-defined primal problem.

**3. Optimized Sample Compute Allocation**

Research demonstrates that with optimized mixed allocation, better accuracy can be achieved than the best single configuration with 128x less compute on code generation and 25x less compute on reasoning tasks.

**4. Heterogeneous Serving**

Recent work emphasizes that joint optimization of model selection, GPU provisioning, tensor parallelism configuration, and workload distribution under coupled resource and SLO constraints remains an important area.

These papers represent the latest approaches to efficiently allocating compute between generation and verification phases during LLM inference.

# Literature Survey: LLM Reasoning and Search Methods at Inference Time (2024--2026)

Below is a structured report of important papers found across the requested topics. For each paper I provide: full title, authors, venue, URL, why it is important, and a one-line summary.

---

## 1. Foundational / Landmark Papers on Test-Time Compute Scaling

### 1.1 Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters
- **Authors:** Charlie Snell, Jaehoon Lee, Kelvin Xu, Aviral Kumar
- **Venue:** arXiv, August 2024 (arXiv:2408.03314)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.03314](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.03314)
- **Why important:** This is arguably the most influential paper establishing that adaptive allocation of test-time compute (via process-based verifiers or distribution updates) can outperform a 14x larger model, achieving 4x efficiency over best-of-N baselines. It introduced the "compute-optimal" test-time scaling framework.
- **One-line summary:** Adaptively allocating inference-time compute per prompt using verifier-guided search can be more effective than scaling model parameters, with a smaller model outperforming a 14x larger one at equivalent FLOPs.

### 1.2 Inference Scaling Laws: An Empirical Analysis of Compute-Optimal Inference for Problem-Solving with Language Models
- **Authors:** Yangzhen Wu, Zhiqing Sun, Shanda Li, Sean Welleck, Yiming Yang
- **Venue:** ICLR 2025 (arXiv:2408.00724)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.00724](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.00724)
- **Why important:** Establishes empirical inference scaling laws showing that smaller models with advanced search algorithms (majority voting, best-of-N, tree search) can outperform larger models, e.g., a 7B model surpassing a 34B model on math reasoning.
- **One-line summary:** Scaling inference compute with appropriate search strategies is often more cost-effective than scaling model parameters, with systematic analysis of greedy, voting, best-of-N, and tree search trade-offs.

### 1.3 s1: Simple Test-Time Scaling
- **Authors:** Niklas Muennighoff, Zitong Yang, Weijia Shi, Xiang Lisa Li, Li Fei-Fei, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Luke Zettlemoyer, Percy Liang, Emmanuel Candes, Tatsunori Hashimoto
- **Venue:** EMNLP 2025 (arXiv:2501.19393)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.19393](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.19393)
- **Why important:** Demonstrated that a simple recipe (1K curated reasoning traces + "budget forcing" to control thinking length) can match or exceed o1-preview on competition math by up to 27%. Highly influential open-source replication of reasoning model capabilities.
- **One-line summary:** Fine-tuning on just 1,000 curated reasoning traces with a budget-forcing mechanism to extend or truncate thinking produces a 32B model that exceeds o1-preview on MATH/AIME benchmarks by up to 27%.

---

## 2. Reasoning Models (o1, o3, DeepSeek-R1, Qwen)

### 2.1 Learning to Reason with LLMs (OpenAI o1)
- **Authors:** OpenAI
- **Venue:** OpenAI Blog, September 2024
- **URL:** [https://openai.com/index/learning-to-reason-with-llms/](https://openai.com/index/learning-to-reason-with-llms/)
- **Why important:** Introduced the paradigm of training models via large-scale RL to produce extended chains of thought at inference time. Kickstarted the "inference-time scaling revolution" and demonstrated that models improve with more thinking time.
- **One-line summary:** OpenAI o1 showed that training with reinforcement learning to produce long internal reasoning chains yields dramatic improvements on math, coding, and science benchmarks, establishing inference-time compute scaling as a major paradigm.

### 2.2 Introducing OpenAI o3 and o4-mini
- **Authors:** OpenAI
- **Venue:** OpenAI Blog, April 2025
- **URL:** [https://openai.com/index/introducing-o3-and-o4-mini/](https://openai.com/index/introducing-o3-and-o4-mini/)
- **Why important:** Demonstrated continued scaling of the inference-time reasoning paradigm: o3 makes 20% fewer major errors than o1, and o3-mini matches o1 at 15x lower cost. Validates that more training compute + more inference compute = continued gains.
- **One-line summary:** o3 extends the reasoning scaling paradigm with an additional order of magnitude in both training and inference compute, delivering 20% fewer errors than o1 while o3-mini achieves o1-level performance at 15x lower cost.

### 2.3 DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
- **Authors:** Daya Guo, Dejian Yang, Haowei Zhang, et al. (200+ authors, DeepSeek-AI)
- **Venue:** Nature, volume 645, pages 633--638 (2025); arXiv:2501.12948
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.12948](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.12948)
- **Why important:** Published in Nature, this paper showed that pure RL (without human-labeled reasoning trajectories) can incentivize emergent reasoning patterns (self-reflection, verification, dynamic strategy adaptation), achieving performance competitive with o1 at a fraction of the training cost. Open-sourced, it became the most influential open reasoning model.
- **One-line summary:** Pure reinforcement learning without human-annotated reasoning traces produces emergent advanced reasoning behaviors (self-reflection, verification) in LLMs, matching frontier proprietary models on math, coding, and STEM benchmarks.

### 2.4 Qwen3 Technical Report
- **Authors:** An Yang, Anfeng Li, Baosong Yang, et al. (60+ authors, Qwen Team)
- **Venue:** arXiv, May 2025 (arXiv:2505.09388)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.09388](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.09388)
- **Why important:** Introduced unified thinking/non-thinking modes in a single model with a "thinking budget" mechanism, eliminating the need for separate reasoning and chat models. Represents the state of the art in flexible inference-time compute allocation.
- **One-line summary:** Qwen3 unifies thinking mode (extended multi-step reasoning) and non-thinking mode (fast responses) within a single model, allowing adaptive inference-time compute allocation via a thinking budget mechanism.

---

## 3. Tree Search and MCTS Methods

### 3.1 Interpretable Contrastive Monte Carlo Tree Search Reasoning
- **Authors:** Zitian Gao, Boye Niu, Xuzheng He, Haotian Xu, Hongzhang Liu, Aiwei Liu, Xuming Hu, Lijie Wen
- **Venue:** ICLR 2025 (arXiv:2410.01707)
- **URL:** [https://openreview.net/forum?id=F4f1afsm3R](https://openreview.net/forum?id=F4f1afsm3R)
- **Why important:** Addresses the key practical barrier to MCTS for LLM reasoning -- speed -- achieving 51.9% speedup per node via speculative decoding, while also introducing an interpretable contrastive reward model. Surpasses o1-mini by 17.4% on Blocksworld.
- **One-line summary:** A speculative-decoding-accelerated MCTS algorithm with an interpretable contrastive reward model achieves 51.9% speed improvement per node and surpasses o1-mini by 17.4% on planning benchmarks.

### 3.2 CMCTS: A Constrained Monte Carlo Tree Search Framework for Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models
- **Authors:** Qingwen Lin, Boyan Xu, Guimin Hu, Zijian Li, Zhifeng Hao, Keli Zhang, Ruichu Cai
- **Venue:** arXiv, February 2025 (arXiv:2502.11169)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.11169](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.11169)
- **Why important:** Introduces constrained action spaces and partial order rules into MCTS, enabling a 7B model to achieve 83.4% average accuracy on math benchmarks, outperforming a 72B baseline by 4.8 points in zero-shot settings.
- **One-line summary:** Constraining the action space and simulation with process reward models and ordering rules allows a 7B model using MCTS to outperform a 72B baseline by 4.8% on mathematical reasoning.

### 3.3 Monte Carlo Tree Search Boosts Reasoning via Iterative Preference Learning
- **Authors:** Yuxi Xie, Anirudh Goyal, Wenyue Zheng, Min-Yen Kan, Timothy P. Lillicrap, Kenji Kawaguchi, Michael Shieh
- **Venue:** arXiv, May 2024 (arXiv:2405.00451)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.00451](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.00451)
- **Why important:** Demonstrates an AlphaZero-style iterative self-improvement loop where MCTS collects step-level preference data for DPO training, achieving +15.8% on ARC-C and +5.9% on GSM8K over SFT baselines. Bridges MCTS and preference learning.
- **One-line summary:** Using MCTS to decompose outcome rewards into step-level preference signals for iterative DPO training yields substantial accuracy gains on arithmetic and commonsense reasoning benchmarks.

### 3.4 ReKG-MCTS: Reinforcing LLM Reasoning on Knowledge Graphs via Training-Free Monte Carlo Tree Search
- **Authors:** Xiaozhuang Song, Shufei Zhang, Tianshu Yu
- **Venue:** ACL 2025 Findings (Vienna, July 2025)
- **URL:** [https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-acl.484/](https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-acl.484/)
- **Why important:** Extends MCTS to structured knowledge graph reasoning without any training, using LLMs for semantic guidance during simulation. Outperforms existing training-free KG reasoning methods.
- **One-line summary:** A training-free MCTS framework that uses LLMs for semantic guidance during tree simulation achieves state-of-the-art results on knowledge graph question answering benchmarks.

---

## 4. Parallel Sampling and Selection Methods

### 4.1 Learning to Reason Across Parallel Samples for LLM Reasoning (Sample Set Aggregator)
- **Authors:** Jianing Qi, Xi Ye, Hao Tang, Zhigang Zhu, Eunsol Choi
- **Venue:** arXiv, June 2025 (arXiv:2506.09014)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09014](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09014)
- **Why important:** Proposes training a small "Sample Set Aggregator" (SSA) model to replace majority voting, achieving +8% over voting on MATH and showing that a 3B SSA surpasses a 72B process reward model.
- **One-line summary:** A compact 3B-parameter model trained with RL to aggregate multiple LLM reasoning samples outperforms majority voting by 8% on MATH and surpasses a 72B process reward model.

### 4.2 Scalable Best-of-N Selection for Large Language Models via Self-Certainty
- **Authors:** Zhewei Kang, Xuandong Zhao, Dawn Song
- **Venue:** NeurIPS 2025 (arXiv:2502.18581)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.18581](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.18581)
- **Why important:** Introduces a lightweight, reward-model-free approach to Best-of-N selection using the LLM's own probability distribution to estimate response quality, scaling effectively and extending to open-ended tasks where self-consistency fails.
- **One-line summary:** Self-certainty leverages intrinsic LLM output probability distributions to select the best response from N samples without an external reward model, scaling efficiently and generalizing to open-ended tasks.

### 4.3 Population-Evolve: A Parallel Sampling and Evolutionary Method for LLM Math Reasoning
- **Authors:** Yanzhi Zhang, Yitong Duan, Zhaoxi Zhang, Jiyan He, Shuxin Zheng
- **Venue:** arXiv, December 2025 (arXiv:2512.19081)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.19081](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.19081)
- **Why important:** Applies genetic algorithm principles to LLM reasoning at inference time, maintaining evolving populations of candidate solutions with iterative refinement -- a novel bridge between evolutionary computation and LLM inference.
- **One-line summary:** A training-free method inspired by genetic algorithms maintains an evolving population of candidate solutions during LLM inference, iteratively refining them for improved mathematical reasoning.

### 4.4 DeepPrune: Parallel Scaling without Inter-trace Redundancy
- **Authors:** Shangqing Tu, Yaxuan Li, Yushi Bai, Lei Hou, Juanzi Li
- **Venue:** ACL 2026 Findings (arXiv:2510.08483)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.08483](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.08483)
- **Why important:** Demonstrates that over 80% of parallel reasoning traces yield identical answers, and introduces a pruning method that reduces tokens by 65--88% while maintaining accuracy within 3 points. Critical for practical deployment of parallel scaling.
- **One-line summary:** A judge-model-based pruning framework eliminates redundant parallel reasoning traces, achieving 65--88% token reduction while maintaining competitive accuracy on challenging math benchmarks.

### 4.5 Inference-Aware Fine-Tuning for Best-of-N Sampling in Large Language Models
- **Authors:** Yinlam Chow, Guy Tennenholtz, Izzeddin Gur, Vincent Zhuang, Bo Dai, Sridhar Thiagarajan, Craig Boutilier, Rishabh Agarwal, Aviral Kumar, Aleksandra Faust
- **Venue:** arXiv, December 2024 (arXiv:2412.15287)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.15287](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.15287)
- **Why important:** Shows that models can be explicitly trained to optimize for Best-of-N inference, learning exploration-exploitation trade-offs that improve BoN32 performance from 26.8% to 30.8% on MATH.
- **One-line summary:** Fine-tuning models to be aware of their inference-time Best-of-N selection process teaches them to balance quality and diversity, yielding improved pass@N and BoN performance.

---

## 5. Verification and Reward Models

### 5.1 Improve Mathematical Reasoning in Language Models by Automated Process Supervision (OmegaPRM)
- **Authors:** Liangchen Luo, Yinxiao Liu, Rosanne Liu, Samrat Phatale, et al.
- **Venue:** arXiv, June 2024 (arXiv:2406.06592)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.06592](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.06592)
- **Why important:** Introduces OmegaPRM, a MCTS-based algorithm that automatically generates 1.5M process supervision annotations without human involvement, boosting Gemini Pro from 51% to 69.4% on MATH500.
- **One-line summary:** An MCTS-based algorithm automatically generates 1.5 million step-level supervision annotations, enabling process reward models that boost Gemini Pro accuracy from 51% to 69.4% on math benchmarks.

### 5.2 Improving LLM Reasoning through Scaling Inference Computation with Collaborative Verification
- **Authors:** Zhenwen Liang, Ye Liu, Tong Niu, Xiangliang Zhang, Yingbo Zhou, Semih Yavuz
- **Venue:** arXiv, October 2024 (arXiv:2410.05318)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.05318](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.05318)
- **Why important:** Introduces collaborative verification combining Chain-of-Thought and Program-of-Thought, where CoT provides stepwise reasoning and PoT provides executable validation, surpassing GPT-4o when paired with Qwen-72B.
- **One-line summary:** Collaborative verification combining CoT step-by-step reasoning with PoT executable validation achieves state-of-the-art results, with Qwen-72B + verifier surpassing GPT-4o on GSM8K and MATH.

### 5.3 Rethinking Optimal Verification Granularity for Compute-Efficient Test-Time Scaling (VG-Search)
- **Authors:** Hao Mark Chen, Guanxi Lu, Yasuyuki Okoshi, Zhiwen Mo, Masato Motomura, Hongxiang Fan
- **Venue:** NeurIPS 2025 (arXiv:2505.11730)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.11730](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.11730)
- **Why important:** Unifies beam search and Best-of-N into a spectrum via a tunable verification granularity parameter, showing that dynamic granularity selection improves accuracy by up to 3.6% while reducing FLOPs by over 52%.
- **One-line summary:** Variable Granularity Search generalizes beam search and Best-of-N through a tunable parameter, achieving up to 3.6% accuracy gains and 52% FLOPs reduction by dynamically selecting verification frequency.

### 5.4 A Survey of Process Reward Models: From Outcome Signals to Process Supervisions for Large Language Models
- **Authors:** Congmin Zheng, Jiachen Zhu, Zhuoying Ou, Yuxiang Chen, et al.
- **Venue:** arXiv, October 2025 (arXiv:2510.08049)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.08049](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.08049)
- **Why important:** Comprehensive survey covering the full PRM lifecycle (data generation, model construction, deployment for test-time scaling and RL), spanning math, code, multimodal, robotics, and agent applications.
- **One-line summary:** A comprehensive survey of process reward models covering their design, training, and deployment across math, code, multimodal, robotics, and agent systems for fine-grained reasoning supervision.

---

## 6. Efficient Reasoning and Compute Budgets

### 6.1 Token-Budget-Aware LLM Reasoning
- **Authors:** Tingxu Han, Zhenting Wang, Chunrong Fang, Shiyu Zhao, Shiqing Ma, Zhenyu Chen
- **Venue:** ACL 2025 Findings (arXiv:2412.18547)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.18547](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.18547)
- **Why important:** Introduces dynamic token budget allocation based on problem complexity, achieving significant token cost reduction with minimal performance loss -- a practical approach to CoT efficiency.
- **One-line summary:** A framework that dynamically adjusts reasoning token budgets based on problem complexity achieves significant token savings with minimal accuracy degradation.

### 6.2 Don't Overthink It: Preferring Shorter Thinking Chains for Improved LLM Reasoning
- **Authors:** Michael Hassid, Gabriel Synnaeve, Yossi Adi, Roy Schwartz
- **Venue:** arXiv, May 2025 (arXiv:2505.17813)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.17813](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.17813)
- **Why important:** Challenges the "more thinking = better" assumption, showing shorter chains are up to 34.5% more accurate than the longest chain for the same question. Introduces short-m@k which reduces tokens by 40% while maintaining performance.
- **One-line summary:** Shorter reasoning chains are up to 34.5% more likely to be correct than longer ones for the same question, and a short-m@k parallel generation method reduces token usage by 40% without sacrificing accuracy.

### 6.3 Scalable Chain of Thoughts via Elastic Reasoning
- **Authors:** Yuhui Xu, Hanze Dong, Lei Wang, Doyen Sahoo, Junnan Li, Caiming Xiong
- **Venue:** arXiv, May 2025 (arXiv:2505.05315)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.05315](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.05315)
- **Why important:** Partitions reasoning into thinking and solution phases with separate budgets, enabling graceful degradation under tight compute constraints while producing more concise reasoning even without constraints.
- **One-line summary:** Elastic Reasoning separates thinking and solution phases with independent token budgets, maintaining strong performance under tight compute constraints by prioritizing solution completion.

### 6.4 Reasoning on a Budget: A Survey of Adaptive and Controllable Test-Time Compute in LLMs
- **Authors:** Mohammad Ali Alomrani, Yingxue Zhang, Derek Li, et al. (17 authors)
- **Venue:** arXiv, July 2025 (arXiv:2507.02076)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.02076](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.02076)
- **Why important:** Dedicated survey on budget-constrained and adaptive test-time compute, categorizing methods into fixed-budget and dynamic approaches. Evaluates major proprietary models on reasoning quality vs. token consumption trade-offs.
- **One-line summary:** A structured survey classifying test-time compute strategies into fixed-budget and adaptive-budget categories, with empirical evaluation of reasoning quality vs. token consumption trade-offs across major models.

## 7. Latent / Continuous Space Reasoning

### 7.1 Scaling up Test-Time Compute with Latent Reasoning: A Recurrent Depth Approach
- **Authors:** Jonas Geiping, Sean McLeish, Neel Jain, John Kirchenbauer, Siddharth Singh, Brian R. Bartoldson, Bhavya Kailkhura, Abhinav Bhatele, Tom Goldstein
- **Venue:** arXiv, February 2025 (arXiv:2502.05171)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.05171](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.05171)
- **Why important:** Proposes reasoning in continuous latent space via a recurrent block that unrolls to arbitrary depth, enabling test-time scaling without generating explicit tokens. A 3.5B model achieves performance of a 50B model at equivalent compute.
- **One-line summary:** A recurrent-depth architecture performs reasoning by iterating in continuous latent space rather than generating tokens, enabling a 3.5B model to match 50B model performance at equivalent compute on reasoning benchmarks.

### 7.2 Parallel Test-Time Scaling for Latent Reasoning Models
- **Authors:** Runyang You, Yongqi Li, Meng Liu, Wenjie Wang, Liqiang Nie, Wenjie Li
- **Venue:** ACL 2026 Main Conference (arXiv:2510.07745)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.07745](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.07745)
- **Why important:** First work to bring parallel test-time scaling to latent reasoning models using Monte Carlo Dropout and Gaussian noise for sampling in continuous space, with a learned latent reward model for trajectory selection.
- **One-line summary:** Introduces parallel test-time scaling for latent-space reasoning models using stochastic sampling strategies and a contrastive latent reward model for trajectory selection.

---

## 8. Comprehensive Survey Papers

### 8.1 What, How, Where, and How Well? A Survey on Test-Time Scaling in Large Language Models
- **Authors:** Qiyuan Zhang, Fuyuan Lyu, Zexu Sun, Lei Wang, Weixu Zhang, Wenyue Hua, Haolun Wu, Zhihan Guo, Yufei Wang, Niklas Muennighoff, Irwin King, Xue Liu, Chen Ma
- **Venue:** arXiv, March 2025 (arXiv:2503.24235)
- **URL:** [https://testtimescaling.github.io/](https://testtimescaling.github.io/)
- **Why important:** The most comprehensive survey on test-time scaling, organized around four dimensions: what to scale (parallel/sequential/hybrid/internal), how (tuning/inference), where (reasoning/general), and how well (performance/efficiency/controllability). Provides practical deployment guidelines.
- **One-line summary:** A comprehensive survey organizing test-time scaling along four dimensions (what/how/where/how well), covering techniques from parallel sampling to latent reasoning with practical deployment guidelines.

### 8.2 A Survey of Scaling in Large Language Model Reasoning
- **Authors:** Zihan Chen, Song Wang, Zhen Tan, Xingbo Fu, Zhenyu Lei, Peng Wang, Huan Liu, Cong Shen, Jundong Li
- **Venue:** arXiv, April 2025 (arXiv:2504.02181)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.02181](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.02181)
- **Why important:** Categorizes scaling for LLM reasoning across multiple dimensions: input size, reasoning steps, interaction rounds, and training optimization. Provides a unified perspective on how different scaling axes contribute to reasoning improvement.
- **One-line summary:** A multi-dimensional survey examining how scaling input size, reasoning steps, interaction rounds, and training optimization each contribute to improving LLM reasoning capabilities.

### 8.3 The Art of Scaling Test-Time Compute for Large Language Models
- **Authors:** Aradhye Agarwal, Ayan Sengupta, Tanmoy Chakraborty
- **Venue:** arXiv, December 2025 (arXiv:2512.02008)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.02008](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.02008)
- **Why important:** Massive empirical study spanning 30+ billion generated tokens across 8 models (7B--235B) and 4 reasoning datasets. Key finding: no single TTS strategy universally dominates, and optimal strategy depends on problem difficulty, model architecture, and compute budget.
- **One-line summary:** An empirical study across 30+ billion tokens, 8 models, and 4 datasets finds that no single test-time scaling strategy universally dominates -- optimal choice depends on problem difficulty and model architecture.

### 8.4 Inference-Time Scaling for Complex Tasks: Where We Stand and What Lies Ahead
- **Authors:** Vidhisha Balachandran, Jingya Chen, Lingjiao Chen, Shivam Garg, Neel Joshi, Yash Lara, John Langford, Besmira Nushi, Vibhav Vineet, Yue Wu, Safoora Yousefi
- **Venue:** arXiv, March 2025 (arXiv:2504.00294)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.00294](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.00294)
- **Why important:** Evaluates 9 foundation models on 8 complex tasks (math, STEM, NP-hard problems, navigation, spatial reasoning), finding that inference-time scaling benefits vary by domain and diminish with problem complexity. Importantly, more tokens do not always help.
- **One-line summary:** Evaluation of 9 models on 8 complex tasks reveals that inference-time scaling advantages vary across domains and diminish as problem complexity increases, with more tokens not always translating to higher accuracy.

## 9. Classic References (Pre-2024, Still Foundational)

### 9.1 Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
- **Authors:** Xuezhi Wang, Jason Wei, Dale Schuurmans, Quoc V. Le, Ed H. Chi, Sharan Narang, Aakanksha Chowdhery, Denny Zhou
- **Venue:** ICLR 2023 (arXiv:2203.11171)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.11171](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.11171)
- **Why important:** The foundational paper on parallel sampling + majority voting for reasoning. Introduced self-consistency decoding which improved CoT by +17.9% on GSM8K. Nearly all subsequent parallel scaling and sample-and-select methods build on this.
- **One-line summary:** Sampling diverse reasoning paths and selecting the most consistent answer via majority voting improves CoT prompting by up to 17.9% on arithmetic reasoning, establishing the foundation for parallel test-time scaling.

### 9.2 Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
- **Authors:** Shunyu Yao, Dian Yu, Jeffrey Zhao, Izhak Shafran, Thomas L. Griffiths, Yuan Cao, Karthik Narasimhan
- **Venue:** NeurIPS 2023
- **URL:** [https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2023/file/271db9922b8d1f4dd7aaef84ed5ac703-Paper-Conference.pdf](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2023/file/271db9922b8d1f4dd7aaef84ed5ac703-Paper-Conference.pdf)
- **Why important:** Introduced the Tree of Thoughts framework generalizing CoT to tree-structured search with self-evaluation, enabling deliberate exploration of multiple reasoning paths via BFS/DFS. Foundation for all subsequent tree search methods in LLM reasoning.
- **One-line summary:** Generalized chain-of-thought to tree-structured search with LLM self-evaluation, enabling deliberate exploration of multiple reasoning paths for complex problem solving.

## Key Themes and Takeaways

1. **Inference-time compute is a new scaling axis:** The 2024--2025 period established that scaling compute at inference time (via search, sampling, or extended thinking) is complementary to -- and sometimes more efficient than -- scaling model parameters (Snell et al., Wu et al.).

2. **Pure RL produces reasoning:** DeepSeek-R1 and OpenAI o1/o3 demonstrated that reinforcement learning alone can elicit emergent reasoning behaviors without explicit human demonstrations of reasoning.

3. **Parallel vs. sequential scaling:** Two broad paradigms emerged -- parallel (sample multiple answers, aggregate) and sequential (think longer, search deeper). Neither universally dominates; optimal strategy depends on task, model, and budget.

4. **Efficiency is the next frontier:** Papers like "Don't Overthink It," Elastic Reasoning, Token-Budget-Aware reasoning, and DeepPrune show that naive compute scaling has severe diminishing returns, and 40--88% of tokens can be saved with intelligent allocation.

5. **Verification is critical:** Process reward models, collaborative verification, and self-certainty methods are essential for realizing the potential of parallel scaling -- the quality of the selector/verifier often matters more than the number of samples.

6. **Latent reasoning is emerging:** Work on reasoning in continuous space (Geiping et al., You et al.) opens a new direction where models reason without generating explicit tokens, potentially offering better compute efficiency.</result>

# Literature Survey: LLM Reasoning and Search Methods at Inference Time (2024--2026)

Below is a structured report of important papers found across the requested topics. For each paper I provide: full title, authors, venue, URL, why it is important, and a one-line summary.

---

## 1. Foundational / Landmark Papers on Test-Time Compute Scaling

### 1.1 Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters
- **Authors:** Charlie Snell, Jaehoon Lee, Kelvin Xu, Aviral Kumar
- **Venue:** arXiv, August 2024 (arXiv:2408.03314)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.03314](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.03314)
- **Why important:** This is arguably the most influential paper establishing that adaptive allocation of test-time compute (via process-based verifiers or distribution updates) can outperform a 14x larger model, achieving 4x efficiency over best-of-N baselines. It introduced the "compute-optimal" test-time scaling framework.
- **One-line summary:** Adaptively allocating inference-time compute per prompt using verifier-guided search can be more effective than scaling model parameters, with a smaller model outperforming a 14x larger one at equivalent FLOPs.

### 1.2 Inference Scaling Laws: An Empirical Analysis of Compute-Optimal Inference for Problem-Solving with Language Models
- **Authors:** Yangzhen Wu, Zhiqing Sun, Shanda Li, Sean Welleck, Yiming Yang
- **Venue:** ICLR 2025 (arXiv:2408.00724)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.00724](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.00724)
- **Why important:** Establishes empirical inference scaling laws showing that smaller models with advanced search algorithms (majority voting, best-of-N, tree search) can outperform larger models, e.g., a 7B model surpassing a 34B model on math reasoning.
- **One-line summary:** Scaling inference compute with appropriate search strategies is often more cost-effective than scaling model parameters, with systematic analysis of greedy, voting, best-of-N, and tree search trade-offs.

### 1.3 s1: Simple Test-Time Scaling
- **Authors:** Niklas Muennighoff, Zitong Yang, Weijia Shi, Xiang Lisa Li, Li Fei-Fei, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Luke Zettlemoyer, Percy Liang, Emmanuel Candes, Tatsunori Hashimoto
- **Venue:** EMNLP 2025 (arXiv:2501.19393)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.19393](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.19393)
- **Why important:** Demonstrated that a simple recipe (1K curated reasoning traces + "budget forcing" to control thinking length) can match or exceed o1-preview on competition math by up to 27%. Highly influential open-source replication of reasoning model capabilities.
- **One-line summary:** Fine-tuning on just 1,000 curated reasoning traces with a budget-forcing mechanism to extend or truncate thinking produces a 32B model that exceeds o1-preview on MATH/AIME benchmarks by up to 27%.

---

## 2. Reasoning Models (o1, o3, DeepSeek-R1, Qwen)

### 2.1 Learning to Reason with LLMs (OpenAI o1)
- **Authors:** OpenAI
- **Venue:** OpenAI Blog, September 2024
- **URL:** [https://openai.com/index/learning-to-reason-with-llms/](https://openai.com/index/learning-to-reason-with-llms/)
- **Why important:** Introduced the paradigm of training models via large-scale RL to produce extended chains of thought at inference time. Kickstarted the "inference-time scaling revolution" and demonstrated that models improve with more thinking time.
- **One-line summary:** OpenAI o1 showed that training with reinforcement learning to produce long internal reasoning chains yields dramatic improvements on math, coding, and science benchmarks, establishing inference-time compute scaling as a major paradigm.

### 2.2 Introducing OpenAI o3 and o4-mini
- **Authors:** OpenAI
- **Venue:** OpenAI Blog, April 2025
- **URL:** [https://openai.com/index/introducing-o3-and-o4-mini/](https://openai.com/index/introducing-o3-and-o4-mini/)
- **Why important:** Demonstrated continued scaling of the inference-time reasoning paradigm: o3 makes 20% fewer major errors than o1, and o3-mini matches o1 at 15x lower cost. Validates that more training compute + more inference compute = continued gains.
- **One-line summary:** o3 extends the reasoning scaling paradigm with an additional order of magnitude in both training and inference compute, delivering 20% fewer errors than o1 while o3-mini achieves o1-level performance at 15x lower cost.

### 2.3 DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
- **Authors:** Daya Guo, Dejian Yang, Haowei Zhang, et al. (200+ authors, DeepSeek-AI)
- **Venue:** Nature, volume 645, pages 633--638 (2025); arXiv:2501.12948
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.12948](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.12948)
- **Why important:** Published in Nature, this paper showed that pure RL (without human-labeled reasoning trajectories) can incentivize emergent reasoning patterns (self-reflection, verification, dynamic strategy adaptation), achieving performance competitive with o1 at a fraction of the training cost. Open-sourced, it became the most influential open reasoning model.
- **One-line summary:** Pure reinforcement learning without human-annotated reasoning traces produces emergent advanced reasoning behaviors (self-reflection, verification) in LLMs, matching frontier proprietary models on math, coding, and STEM benchmarks.

### 2.4 Qwen3 Technical Report
- **Authors:** An Yang, Anfeng Li, Baosong Yang, et al. (60+ authors, Qwen Team)
- **Venue:** arXiv, May 2025 (arXiv:2505.09388)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.09388](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.09388)
- **Why important:** Introduced unified thinking/non-thinking modes in a single model with a "thinking budget" mechanism, eliminating the need for separate reasoning and chat models. Represents the state of the art in flexible inference-time compute allocation.
- **One-line summary:** Qwen3 unifies thinking mode (extended multi-step reasoning) and non-thinking mode (fast responses) within a single model, allowing adaptive inference-time compute allocation via a thinking budget mechanism.

## 3. Tree Search and MCTS Methods

### 3.1 Interpretable Contrastive Monte Carlo Tree Search Reasoning
- **Authors:** Zitian Gao, Boye Niu, Xuzheng He, Haotian Xu, Hongzhang Liu, Aiwei Liu, Xuming Hu, Lijie Wen
- **Venue:** ICLR 2025 (arXiv:2410.01707)
- **URL:** [https://openreview.net/forum?id=F4f1afsm3R](https://openreview.net/forum?id=F4f1afsm3R)
- **Why important:** Addresses the key practical barrier to MCTS for LLM reasoning -- speed -- achieving 51.9% speedup per node via speculative decoding, while also introducing an interpretable contrastive reward model. Surpasses o1-mini by 17.4% on Blocksworld.
- **One-line summary:** A speculative-decoding-accelerated MCTS algorithm with an interpretable contrastive reward model achieves 51.9% speed improvement per node and surpasses o1-mini by 17.4% on planning benchmarks.

### 3.2 CMCTS: A Constrained Monte Carlo Tree Search Framework for Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models
- **Authors:** Qingwen Lin, Boyan Xu, Guimin Hu, Zijian Li, Zhifeng Hao, Keli Zhang, Ruichu Cai
- **Venue:** arXiv, February 2025 (arXiv:2502.11169)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.11169](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.11169)
- **Why important:** Introduces constrained action spaces and partial order rules into MCTS, enabling a 7B model to achieve 83.4% average accuracy on math benchmarks, outperforming a 72B baseline by 4.8 points in zero-shot settings.
- **One-line summary:** Constraining the action space and simulation with process reward models and ordering rules allows a 7B model using MCTS to outperform a 72B baseline by 4.8% on mathematical reasoning.

### 3.3 Monte Carlo Tree Search Boosts Reasoning via Iterative Preference Learning
- **Authors:** Yuxi Xie, Anirudh Goyal, Wenyue Zheng, Min-Yen Kan, Timothy P. Lillicrap, Kenji Kawaguchi, Michael Shieh
- **Venue:** arXiv, May 2024 (arXiv:2405.00451)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.00451](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.00451)
- **Why important:** Demonstrates an AlphaZero-style iterative self-improvement loop where MCTS collects step-level preference data for DPO training, achieving +15.8% on ARC-C and +5.9% on GSM8K over SFT baselines. Bridges MCTS and preference learning.
- **One-line summary:** Using MCTS to decompose outcome rewards into step-level preference signals for iterative DPO training yields substantial accuracy gains on arithmetic and commonsense reasoning benchmarks.

### 3.4 ReKG-MCTS: Reinforcing LLM Reasoning on Knowledge Graphs via Training-Free Monte Carlo Tree Search
- **Authors:** Xiaozhuang Song, Shufei Zhang, Tianshu Yu
- **Venue:** ACL 2025 Findings (Vienna, July 2025)
- **URL:** [https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-acl.484/](https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-acl.484/)
- **Why important:** Extends MCTS to structured knowledge graph reasoning without any training, using LLMs for semantic guidance during simulation. Outperforms existing training-free KG reasoning methods.
- **One-line summary:** A training-free MCTS framework that uses LLMs for semantic guidance during tree simulation achieves state-of-the-art results on knowledge graph question answering benchmarks.

## 4. Parallel Sampling and Selection Methods

### 4.1 Learning to Reason Across Parallel Samples for LLM Reasoning (Sample Set Aggregator)
- **Authors:** Jianing Qi, Xi Ye, Hao Tang, Zhigang Zhu, Eunsol Choi
- **Venue:** arXiv, June 2025 (arXiv:2506.09014)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09014](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09014)
- **Why important:** Proposes training a small "Sample Set Aggregator" (SSA) model to replace majority voting, achieving +8% over voting on MATH and showing that a 3B SSA surpasses a 72B process reward model.
- **One-line summary:** A compact 3B-parameter model trained with RL to aggregate multiple LLM reasoning samples outperforms majority voting by 8% on MATH and surpasses a 72B process reward model.

### 4.2 Scalable Best-of-N Selection for Large Language Models via Self-Certainty
- **Authors:** Zhewei Kang, Xuandong Zhao, Dawn Song
- **Venue:** NeurIPS 2025 (arXiv:2502.18581)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.18581](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.18581)
- **Why important:** Introduces a lightweight, reward-model-free approach to Best-of-N selection using the LLM's own probability distribution to estimate response quality, scaling effectively and extending to open-ended tasks where self-consistency fails.
- **One-line summary:** Self-certainty leverages intrinsic LLM output probability distributions to select the best response from N samples without an external reward model, scaling efficiently and generalizing to open-ended tasks.

### 4.3 Population-Evolve: A Parallel Sampling and Evolutionary Method for LLM Math Reasoning
- **Authors:** Yanzhi Zhang, Yitong Duan, Zhaoxi Zhang, Jiyan He, Shuxin Zheng
- **Venue:** arXiv, December 2025 (arXiv:2512.19081)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.19081](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.19081)
- **Why important:** Applies genetic algorithm principles to LLM reasoning at inference time, maintaining evolving populations of candidate solutions with iterative refinement -- a novel bridge between evolutionary computation and LLM inference.
- **One-line summary:** A training-free method inspired by genetic algorithms maintains an evolving population of candidate solutions during LLM inference, iteratively refining them for improved mathematical reasoning.

- **Authors:** Shangqing Tu, Yaxuan Li, Yushi Bai, Lei Hou, Juanzi Li
- **Venue:** ACL 2026 Findings (arXiv:2510.08483)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.08483](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.08483)
- **Why important:** Demonstrates that over 80% of parallel reasoning traces yield identical answers, and introduces a pruning method that reduces tokens by 65--88% while maintaining accuracy within 3 points. Critical for practical deployment of parallel scaling.
- **One-line summary:** A judge-model-based pruning framework eliminates redundant parallel reasoning traces, achieving 65--88% token reduction while maintaining competitive accuracy on challenging math benchmarks.

### 4.5 Inference-Aware Fine-Tuning for Best-of-N Sampling in Large Language Models
- **Authors:** Yinlam Chow, Guy Tennenholtz, Izzeddin Gur, Vincent Zhuang, Bo Dai, Sridhar Thiagarajan, Craig Boutilier, Rishabh Agarwal, Aviral Kumar, Aleksandra Faust
- **Venue:** arXiv, December 2024 (arXiv:2412.15287)
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.15287](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.15287)
- **Why important:** Shows that models can be explicitly trained to optimize for Best-of-N inference, learning exploration-exploitation trade-offs that improve BoN32 performance from 26.8% to 30.8% on MATH.
- **One-line summary:** Fine-tuning models to be aware of their inference-time Best-of-N selection process teaches them to balance quality and diversity, yielding improved pass@N and BoN performance.

- **Authors:** Liangchen Luo, Yinxiao Liu, Rosanne Liu, Samrat Phatale, et al.

- **Authors:** Zhenwen Liang, Ye Liu, Tong Niu, Xiangliang Zhang, Yingbo Zhou, Semih Yavuz

- **Why important:** Introduces collaborative verification combining Chain-of-Thought and Program-of-Thought, where CoT provides stepwise reasoning and PoT provides executable validation, surpassing GPT-4o when paired with Qwen-72B.
- **One-line summary:** Collaborative verification combining CoT step-by-step reasoning with PoT executable validation achieves state-of-the-art results, with Qwen-72B + verifier surpassing GPT-4o on GSM8K and MATH.

- **Authors:** Hao Mark Chen, Guanxi Lu, Yasuyuki Okoshi, Zhiwen Mo, Masato Motomura, Hongxiang Fan

- **Authors:** Michael Hassid, Gabriel Synnaeve, Yossi Adi, Roy Schwartz

**Authors:** Jianyuan Zhong, Zeju Li, Zhijian Xu, Xiangyu Wen, Kezhi Li, Qiang Xu

**Venue:** arXiv Computer Science - Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

**Abstract Summary:**

The paper addresses the challenge of balancing accuracy and efficiency in LLM reasoning. Researchers propose FlexiVe, a generative verifier that "flexibly balances computational resources between rapid, reliable fast thinking and meticulous slow thinking." The Solve-Detect-Verify pipeline intelligently identifies when solutions are complete and triggers verification with targeted feedback. The approach demonstrates improved performance on mathematical reasoning benchmarks including AIME 2024, AIME 2025, and CNMO, outperforming methods like self-consistency while improving inference efficiency.

**Key Innovation:** A flexible budget allocation strategy for verification that avoids the computational overhead of sophisticated verification methods while maintaining reliability.

# OSCA Paper Details

**Full Title:** "Scaling LLM Inference with Optimized Sample Compute Allocation"

**Authors:** Kexun Zhang, Shang Zhou, Danqing Wang, William Yang Wang, Lei Li

**Abstract:** The paper addresses finding optimal computational resource distribution across different sampling configurations during LLM inference. The researchers propose OSCA, which "Optimizes Sample Compute Allocation by finding an optimal mix of different inference configurations." Their experiments demonstrate significant efficiency gains: achieving superior accuracy with 128x reduced computation on code generation tasks and 25x less compute on reasoning benchmarks compared to single-configuration approaches. The method also extends to multi-turn workflows, improving performance on SWE-Bench with 3x computational savings.

Here is the structured literature survey on **per-instance adaptive co-optimization of generation and verification compute for LLM inference**.

---

## SEED PAPERS

### 1. When To Solve, When To Verify: Compute-Optimal Problem Solving and Generative Verification for LLM Reasoning
- **Authors:** Nishad Singhi, Hritik Bansal, Arian Hosseini, Aditya Grover, Kai-Wei Chang, Marcus Rohrbach, Anna Rohrbach
- **Venue:** arXiv:2504.01005, April 2025 (revised October 2025); submitted to COLM 2025
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.01005](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.01005)
- **Summary:** Derives inference scaling laws showing that compute-optimal inference favors scaling solution generation more aggressively than verification; Self-Consistency outperforms GenRM at lower budgets while GenRM excels at higher budgets, with GenRM requiring up to 8x the inference compute to match SC.

### 2. Scaling Test-Time Compute Without Verification or RL is Suboptimal
- **Authors:** Amrith Setlur, Nived Rajaraman, Sergey Levine, Aviral Kumar
- **Venue:** arXiv:2502.12118, February 2025; ICLR 2025 Workshop
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.12118](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.12118)
- **Summary:** Proves formally using anti-concentration theory that verifier-based (VB) methods via RL/search are far superior to verifier-free (VF) distillation approaches for scaling test-time compute, with the performance gap widening as budgets grow; corroborated empirically on 3B/8B/32B LLMs.

### 3. Rethinking Optimal Verification Granularity for Compute-Efficient Test-Time Scaling (VG-Search)
- **Authors:** Hao Mark Chen, Guanxi Lu, Yasuyuki Okoshi, Zhiwen Mo, Masato Motomura, Hongxiang Fan
- **Venue:** arXiv:2505.11730, May 2025; NeurIPS 2025
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.11730](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.11730)
- **Summary:** Introduces Variable Granularity Search (VG-Search) that generalizes beam search and Best-of-N via a tunable granularity parameter controlling verification frequency; adaptive granularity yields up to 3.6% accuracy gains over Best-of-N while reducing FLOPs by over 52%.

### 4. Sampling-Efficient Test-Time Scaling: Self-Estimating the Best-of-N Sampling in Early Decoding (ST-BoN)
- **Authors:** Yiming Wang, Pei Zhang, Siyuan Huang, Baosong Yang, Zhuosheng Zhang, Fei Huang, Rui Wang
- **Venue:** arXiv:2503.01422, March 2025; NeurIPS 2025 Spotlight
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.01422](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.01422)
- **Summary:** Proposes Self-Truncation Best-of-N (ST-BoN) that identifies the most promising decoding path early and truncates suboptimal ones without requiring reward models; reduces GPU memory by 80%, latency by 50%, and achieves 70-80% compute savings at equivalent accuracy.

---

## CLOSELY RELATED FOLLOW-UP AND CITING WORK

### Foundational / Precursor Papers

**5. Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters**
- **Authors:** Charlie Snell, Jaehoon Lee, Kelvin Xu, Aviral Kumar
- **Venue:** arXiv:2408.03314, August 2024; ICLR 2025
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.03314](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.03314)
- **Summary:** Foundational work showing that a compute-optimal strategy allocating test-time compute adaptively per prompt improves efficiency by 4x over best-of-N, and enables a smaller model to outperform a 14x larger model in FLOPs-matched evaluation.

**6. Inference Scaling Laws: An Empirical Analysis of Compute-Optimal Inference for Problem-Solving with Language Models**
- **Authors:** Yangzhen Wu, Zhiqing Sun, Shanda Li, Sean Welleck, Yiming Yang
- **Venue:** arXiv:2408.00724, August 2024; ICLR 2025
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.00724](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.00724)
- **Summary:** Empirically derives inference scaling laws across greedy search, majority voting, best-of-N, weighted voting, and tree search; finds that smaller models + advanced inference algorithms offer Pareto-optimal cost-performance tradeoffs vs. scaling model parameters.

### Per-Instance Adaptive Compute Allocation

**7. LATTS: Locally Adaptive Test-Time Scaling**
- **Authors:** Theo Uscidda, Matthew Trager, Michael Kleinman, Aditya Chattopadhyay, Wei Xia, Stefano Soatto
- **Venue:** arXiv:2509.20368, September 2025
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.20368](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.20368)
- **Summary:** Allocates variable compute across generation steps using a verifier-based acceptance criterion to decide per-step whether to resample, backtrack, restart, or stop, adjusting effort based on local difficulty; achieves superior accuracy-compute tradeoffs vs. uniform methods.

**8. Adaptive Test-Time Compute Allocation for Reasoning LLMs via Constrained Policy Optimization**
- **Authors:** Zhiyuan Zhai, Bingcong Li, Bingnan Xiao, Ming Li, Xin Wang
- **Venue:** arXiv:2604.14853, April 2026
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.14853](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.14853)
- **Summary:** Formalizes test-time compute allocation as a constrained optimization problem (maximize accuracy subject to average compute budget) with Lagrangian decomposition into per-instance sub-problems; achieves up to 12.8% relative accuracy improvement on MATH.

**9. What If We Allocate Test-Time Compute Adaptively?**
- **Authors:** Ahsan Bilal, Ahmed Mohsin, Muhammad Umer, Ali Subhan, Hassan Rizwan, Ayesha Mohsin, Dean Hougen
- **Venue:** arXiv:2602.01070, February 2026
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.01070](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.01070)
- **Summary:** Framework using a process reward model to guide both trajectory generation within iterations and selection across iterations for dynamic per-instance compute allocation; substantial improvements on MATH-500, AIME24, and AMO-Bench.

**10. Adaptive Test-Time Compute Allocation via Learned Heuristics over Categorical Structure**
- **Authors:** Shuhui Qu
- **Venue:** arXiv:2602.03975, February 2026
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.03975](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.03975)
- **Summary:** Allocates verification according to state-local uncertainty rather than uniform rules using deterministic gating and a hybrid scoring mechanism; achieves higher accuracy than best-of-N, majority voting, and beam search while using 44% fewer verifier calls on MATH.

**11. Adaptive Test-Time Compute Allocation with Evolving In-Context Demonstrations**
- **Authors:** Bowen Zuo, Dongruo Zhou, Yinglun Zhu
- **Venue:** arXiv:2604.21018, April 2026
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.21018](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.21018)
- **Summary:** Jointly adapts where computation is spent and how generation is performed, concentrating further compute on unresolved queries while reshaping generation distributions through evolving in-context demonstrations.

**12. Anytime Verified Agents: Adaptive Compute Allocation for Reliable LLM Reasoning under Budget Constraints**
- **Authors:** (Multiple; see OpenReview)
- **Venue:** OpenReview, April 2026
- **URL:** [https://openreview.net/forum?id=JMDCMf7mlF](https://openreview.net/forum?id=JMDCMf7mlF)
- **Summary:** Dynamically allocates compute across search, sampling, and verification within a user-specified budget using calibrated uncertainty estimation, value-of-information-guided search expansion, and selective verification cascades with early exits.

### Verification Design and Tradeoffs

**13. Budget-aware Test-time Scaling via Discriminative Verification**
- **Authors:** Kyle Montgomery, Sijun Tan, Yuqi Chen, Siyuan Zhuang, Tianjun Zhang, Raluca Ada Popa, Chenguang Wang
- **Venue:** arXiv:2510.14913, October 2025
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.14913](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.14913)
- **Summary:** Shows hybrid discriminative verification (combining verifier scores with self-consistency) surpasses generative verifiers under practical compute budgets, achieving up to 15.3% higher accuracy on AIME2025 at matched cost.

**14. Pushing Test-Time Scaling Limits of Deep Search with Asymmetric Verification**
- **Authors:** Weihao Zeng, Keqing He, Chuqiao Kuang, Xiaoguang Li, Junxian He
- **Venue:** arXiv:2510.06135, October 2025
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.06135](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.06135)
- **Summary:** Exploits asymmetric verification (verifying is substantially easier than generating) in deep search agents; on BrowseComp, verification requires only ~18 tool calls vs. ~75 for generation.

**15. Variation in Verification: Understanding Verification Dynamics in Large Language Models**
- **Authors:** Yefan Zhou, Austin Xu, Yilun Zhou, Janvijay Singh, Jiang Gui, Shafiq Joty
- **Venue:** arXiv:2509.17995, September 2025
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.17995](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.17995)
- **Summary:** Systematically analyzes verification dynamics across problem difficulty, generator capability, and verifier capability on 12 benchmarks with 14 models; finds weak generators can nearly match stronger ones post-verification (gap shrinks by 75.5%).

**16. Multi-Agent Verification: Scaling Test-Time Compute with Multiple Verifiers**
- **Authors:** Shalev Lifshitz, Sheila A. McIlraith, Yilun Du
- **Venue:** arXiv:2502.20379, February 2025
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.20379](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.20379)
- **Summary:** Proposes scaling the number of verifiers as a new dimension; BoN-MAV combines best-of-N with multiple aspect verifiers, demonstrating weak-to-strong generalization and self-improvement.

**17. Trust but Verify! A Survey on Verification Design for Test-time Scaling**
- **Authors:** V. Venktesh et al.
- **Venue:** arXiv:2508.16665, August 2025
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.16665](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.16665)
- **Summary:** Comprehensive survey covering prompt-based, discriminative, and generative verifiers for process/outcome verification and their roles in test-time scaling.

### Process and Generative Reward Models

**18. GenPRM: Scaling Test-Time Compute of Process Reward Models via Generative Reasoning**
- **Authors:** Jian Zhao, Runze Liu, Kaiyan Zhang, Zhimu Zhou, Junqi Gao, Dong Li, Jiafei Lyu, Zhouyi Qian, Biqing Qi, Xiu Li, Bowen Zhou
- **Venue:** arXiv:2504.00891, April 2025; AAAI 2026
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.00891](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.00891)
- **Summary:** Redefines process supervision as a generative task with CoT reasoning and code verification; 1.5B GenPRM outperforms GPT-4o and 7B GenPRM surpasses Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-72B on ProcessBench.

**19. Process Reward Models That Think (ThinkPRM)**
- **Authors:** Mukul Bhatt et al.
- **Venue:** arXiv:2504.16828, April 2025
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.16828](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.16828)
- **Summary:** Long-CoT verifier fine-tuned on orders of magnitude fewer process labels than discriminative PRMs using only 8K step labels; surpasses discriminative verifiers trained on full PRM800K by 8% (GPQA-Diamond) and 4.5% (LiveCodeBench).

### Scaling Laws and Joint Optimization

**20. Scaling LLM Inference with Optimized Sample Compute Allocation (OSCA)**
- **Authors:** Kexun Zhang, Shang Zhou, Danqing Wang, William Yang Wang, Lei Li
- **Venue:** arXiv:2410.22480, October 2024; NAACL 2025
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.22480](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.22480)
- **Summary:** Optimizes sample compute allocation by finding an optimal mix of inference configurations (model, temperature, etc.); achieves accuracy better than best single config with 128x less compute on code generation and 25x less on reasoning.

**21. Test-Time Scaling Makes Overtraining Compute-Optimal (T-squared Scaling)**
- **Authors:** Nicholas Roberts, Sung-Dae Cho, Zhiqi Gao, Tzu-Heng Huang, Albert Wu, Gabriel Orlanski, Avi Trost, Kelly Buchanan, Aws Albarghouthi, Frederic Sala
- **Venue:** arXiv:2604.01411, April 2026
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.01411](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.01411)
- **Summary:** Derives Train-to-Test (T-squared) scaling laws jointly optimizing model size, training tokens, and inference samples; finds radical overtraining of smaller models becomes compute-optimal when accounting for repeated sampling at inference.

**22. Predicting and Improving Test-Time Scaling Laws via Reward Tail-Guided Search**
- **Authors:** (Multiple authors)
- **Venue:** arXiv:2602.01485, February 2026
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.01485](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.01485)
- **Summary:** Proposes Scaling-Law Guided (SLG) Search that dynamically allocates compute by estimating the tail distribution of rewards; achieves expected rewards requiring polynomially larger compute under BoN, with vanishing regret vs. perfect-information oracles.

**23. Scaling over Scaling: Exploring Test-Time Scaling Pareto in Large Reasoning Models**
- **Authors:** Jian Wang, Boyan Zhu, Chak Tou Leong, Yongqi Li, Wenjie Li
- **Venue:** arXiv:2505.20522, May 2025
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.20522](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.20522)
- **Summary:** Introduces Test-Time Scaling Performance Model (TTSPM) deriving saturation points for both parallel and sequential scaling paradigms; identifies thresholds beyond which additional computation yields diminishing returns.

### Training for Efficient Test-Time Compute

**24. e3: Learning to Explore Enables Extrapolation of Test-Time Compute for LLMs**
- **Authors:** Amrith Setlur, Matthew Y. R. Yang, Charlie Snell, Jeremy Greer, Ian Wu, Virginia Smith, Max Simchowitz, Aviral Kumar
- **Venue:** arXiv:2506.09026, June 2025; ICLR 2026

- **Authors:** Yuxiao Qu, Matthew Y. R. Yang, Amrith Setlur, Lewis Tunstall, Edward E. Beeching, Ruslan Salakhutdinov, Aviral Kumar
- **Venue:** arXiv:2503.07572, March 2025
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.07572](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.07572)

- **Authors:** Feng Chen, Allan Raventos, Nan Cheng, Surya Ganguli, Shaul Druckmann
- **Venue:** arXiv:2502.07154, February 2025; NeurIPS 2025

- **Authors:** Xinglin Wang et al.
- **Venue:** arXiv:2506.15707, June 2025; NeurIPS 2025
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.15707](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.15707)

- **Authors:** Yue Yu, Qiwei Di, Quanquan Gu, Dongruo Zhou
- **Venue:** arXiv:2512.04558, December 2025
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.04558](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.04558)

- **Authors:** Audrey Huang, Adam Block, Qinghua Liu, Nan Jiang, Akshay Krishnamurthy, Dylan J. Foster

- **Authors:** (Multiple authors)

- **Authors:** Zili Wang, Tianyu Zhang, Haoli Bai, Lu Hou, Xianzhi Yu, Wulong Liu, Shiming Xiang, Lei Zhu
- **Venue:** arXiv:2505.19634, May 2025; EMNLP 2025 Findings
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.19634](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.19634)
- **Summary:** Optimizes test-time scaling from a latency-sensitive perspective using branch-wise and sequence-wise parallelism; a 32B model reaches 82.3% on MATH-500 within 1 minute.

- **Authors:** Xi Wang, Anushri Suresh, Alvin Zhang, Rishi More, William Jurayj, Benjamin Van Durme, Mehrdad Farajtabar, Daniel Khashabi, Eric Nalisnick
- **Venue:** arXiv:2602.03814, February 2026
- **URL:** [https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.03814](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.03814)
- **Summary:** Reframes compute budget allocation as distribution-free risk control with upper (confidence-based stopping) and lower (preemptive stopping for unsolvable instances) thresholds, minimizing compute while guaranteeing a user-specified error rate.

**Full Title:** Wider or Deeper? Scaling LLM Inference-Time Compute with Adaptive Branching Tree Search

**Authors:** Yuichi Inoue, Kou Misaki, Yuki Imajuku, So Kuroki, Taishi Nakamura, Takuya Akiba

# Meta Reinforcement Fine-Tuning Paper Details

**Full Title:** "Optimizing Test-Time Compute via Meta Reinforcement Fine-Tuning"

**Authors:** Yuxiao Qu, Matthew Y. R. Yang, Amrith Setlur, Lewis Tunstall, Edward Emanuel Beeching, Ruslan Salakhutdinov, and Aviral Kumar

**Venue:** arXiv (Computer Science > Machine Learning), submitted March 10, 2025
- **Identifier:** arXiv:2503.07572 [cs.LG]
- **DOI:** https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2503.07572

**Abstract Summary:** The paper addresses how language models can better leverage computational resources during inference. Rather than relying solely on conventional reinforcement learning with binary rewards or fine-tuning on search trajectories, the authors reframe test-time compute optimization as a meta-reinforcement learning challenge. They propose measuring effectiveness through cumulative regret across output tokens and introduce MRT (Meta Reinforcement Fine-Tuning), which combines a dense progress-based reward signal with outcome-based rewards. The approach emphasizes balancing exploration and exploitation throughout token generation, yielding "2-3x relative gain in performance and roughly a 1.5x gain in token efficiency for math reasoning compared to outcome-reward RL."
